questions.question: Can a non-executive director of a private sector bank give instructions directly to bank employees or branch managers on operational matters?
questions.answer: No, a non-executive director has no individual power to act on behalf of the bank or give directions to employees; any instructions must be routed through the MD&CEO or CEO.
questions.evidence: a NED as an individual, shall have no power to act on behalf of the PVB nor can they give any direction to the employees of the PVB on behalf of the management. A NED shall desist from sending any instructions to the individual officers on any matters

questions.question: What must a non-executive director do if they have a direct or indirect interest in a contract or loan being discussed by the board of a private sector bank?
questions.answer: The director must disclose the nature of their interest to the board as soon as possible and must not vote on that contract, loan, arrangement, or proposal unless their presence is required by other directors to elicit information.
questions.evidence: a NED who is directly or indirectly concerned or interested in any contract, loan, arrangement or proposal entered into or proposed to be entered by or on behalf of the banking company shall, as soon as possible after the relevant circumstances have come to their knowledge, disclose the nature of their interest to the Board

unanswerable.question: Within how many calendar days must a non-executive director disclose their interest in a contract or loan after becoming aware of it?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states disclosure must be made 'as soon as possible' but does not specify a numeric deadline or calendar day limit.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank charge fees for additional facilities offered in a Basic Savings Bank Deposit account?
questions.answer: Yes, a commercial bank may provide additional facilities in a BSBD account with or without charges, as long as it is done in a non-discretionary and non-discriminatory manner with transparent disclosure.
questions.evidence: A bank may provide additional facilities beyond the above minimum in a BSBD account, with or without charges, in a non-discretionary and non-discriminatory manner with transparent disclosure to the customer.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank allowed to require a minimum balance in a BSBD account when the customer opts for additional facilities?
questions.answer: No, the bank shall not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account even when additional facilities are availed.
questions.evidence: However, while doing so, the bank shall not require the customer to maintain a minimum balance in the BSBD account.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of additional facilities a commercial bank can offer in a BSBD account under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any limit on the number of additional facilities a bank may provide.

questions.question: Does a commercial bank's outsourcing arrangement reduce or alter its customers' legal rights against the bank?
questions.answer: No, outsourcing arrangements cannot affect customers' rights against the bank, including their ability to seek redressal under applicable laws.
questions.evidence: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

questions.question: Can customers of a commercial bank still pursue redressal for issues arising from outsourced services?
questions.answer: Yes, customers retain their ability to obtain redressal under relevant laws regardless of any outsourcing arrangement the bank has entered into.
questions.evidence: Outsourcing arrangements entered into by a bank shall not affect the rights of its customers against the bank, including the ability of the customers to obtain redressal as applicable under relevant laws.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time limit a commercial bank has to resolve a customer complaint related to an outsourced service?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that outsourcing must not affect customers' redressal rights under relevant laws, but it does not specify any time limit, deadline, or procedural timeline for complaint resolution.

questions.question: Does the Reserve Bank of India have the final authority to interpret the fraud risk management directions for NBFCs?
questions.answer: Yes, the RBI's interpretation of any provision of these directions is final and binding.
questions.evidence: the interpretation of any provision of these Directions given by RBI shall be final and binding.

questions.question: What is the minimum fraud amount that an NBFC is advised to report to law enforcement agencies?
questions.answer: An NBFC is advised to mandatorily report fraud incidents involving ₹1 lakh or more to law enforcement agencies.
questions.evidence: The Applicable NBFC is, however, advised to mandatorily report incidents of fraud involving an amount of ₹1 lakh or more to LEAs.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an NBFC report a fraud of ₹1 lakh or more to law enforcement agencies after detection?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies the monetary threshold for mandatory reporting to law enforcement agencies but does not prescribe any time limit or deadline for such reporting.

questions.question: Which regulatory framework governs the capital computation and credit risk mitigation benefits for individual loan assets covered by a default loss guarantee?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 govern capital computation and credit risk mitigation benefits for such loan assets.
questions.evidence: Capital computation, i.e., computation of exposure and application of Credit Risk Mitigation benefits on individual loan assets in the portfolio shall continue to be governed by the Reserve Bank of India (Non- Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: If an NBFC acts as a default loss guarantee provider, what capital deduction must it make for the outstanding guarantee amount?
questions.answer: The NBFC must deduct the full amount of the outstanding default loss guarantee from its capital.
questions.evidence: In case, DLG provider is an NBFC, it shall deduct full amount of the DLG which is outstanding from its capital.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum capital adequacy ratio an NBFC must maintain after deducting the outstanding default loss guarantee amount from its capital?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that the NBFC must deduct the full outstanding DLG amount from its capital, but does not specify any minimum capital adequacy ratio or threshold that must be maintained after the deduction.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of board members required to form the Nomination Committee for an NBFC-Account Aggregator?
questions.answer: The Nomination Committee must consist of at least three members of the Board of Directors.
questions.evidence: consisting of not less than three members of its Board of Directors

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Nomination Committee that an NBFC-Account Aggregator must establish?
questions.answer: The committee is responsible for ensuring the 'fit and proper' status of proposed and existing directors.
questions.evidence: to ensure 'fit and proper' status of proposed/ existing directors

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of commencement of business must an NBFC-Account Aggregator constitute its Nomination Committee?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any timeline or deadline for forming the Nomination Committee.

questions.question: Can an NBFC enter into a default loss guarantee arrangement with any entity, or are there restrictions on the counterparty?
questions.answer: An NBFC may only enter into DLG arrangements with a lending service provider (LSP) or another lender that is engaged as an LSP.
questions.evidence: An NBFC may enter into DLG arrangements only with an LSP / other lender engaged as an LSP.

questions.question: What are the incorporation requirements for a lending service provider that wants to provide a default loss guarantee to an NBFC?
questions.answer: The LSP providing DLG must be incorporated as a company under the Companies Act, 2013.
questions.evidence: Further, the LSP providing DLG shall be incorporated as a company under the Companies Act, 2013.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum net owned fund requirement for an LSP to be eligible as a DLG provider under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any minimum net owned fund or capital requirement for LSPs acting as DLG providers.

questions.question: What must an NBFC-MFI do regarding the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities when computing its capital?
questions.answer: An NBFC-MFI must follow the provisions of the RBI's Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions, 2025 for the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for capital computation.
questions.evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall also adhere to provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 on treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for computation of capital.

questions.question: Which regulatory framework governs how an NBFC-MFI accounts for deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities in its capital adequacy calculation?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 governs the treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for capital computation by an NBFC-MFI.
questions.evidence: An NBFC-MFI shall also adhere to provisions of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directions, 2025 on treatment of deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities for computation of capital.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum percentage of deferred tax assets that an NBFC-MFI can include in its Tier 1 capital under these directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that NBFC-MFIs must adhere to the Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy Directions, 2025 for treatment of deferred tax items, but does not specify any numerical limits, percentages, or Tier 1 capital inclusion rules within this paragraph.

questions.question: What policy must a commercial bank formulate before publishing photographs of wilful defaulters under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters) Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: The bank must formulate a non-discriminatory, board-approved policy that clearly sets out the criteria for publishing photographs of persons classified and declared as wilful defaulters.
questions.evidence: A bank shall formulate a non-discriminatory board-approved policy that clearly sets out the criteria based on which the photographs of persons classified and declared as wilful defaulter shall be published.

questions.question: What covenant must a commercial bank incorporate in credit facility agreements regarding persons listed as wilful defaulters under the RBI Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: The bank must include a covenant that the borrower will not induct any person whose name appears in the List of Wilful Defaulters onto its board or as a person in charge of management, and must take steps to remove such a person if found.
questions.evidence: A bank shall incorporate a covenant in the agreement while extending credit facility to a borrower that it shall not induct a person whose name appears in the LWD on its board or as a person in charge and responsible for the management of the affairs of the entity.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum outstanding amount that triggers the classification of a borrower as a wilful defaulter under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any monetary threshold for wilful defaulter classification; it only describes measures applicable after a person or entity has already been classified and declared as a wilful defaulter.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank do regarding disclosure of penalty components for FCNR(B) term deposits at the time of acceptance?
questions.answer: The bank must clearly bring the penalty components to the depositor's notice at acceptance; otherwise, the bank bears any exchange loss from premature withdrawal.
questions.evidence: The components of penalty shall be clearly brought to the notice of the depositors at the time of acceptance of the deposits. If not, the exchange loss arising out of premature withdrawal shall be borne by the bank.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank allowed to charge a penalty when an NRI prematurely converts FCNR(B) deposits into an RFC Account upon returning to India?
questions.answer: No, the bank is prohibited from levying any penalty in such cases.
questions.evidence: No penalties shall be levied in the case of premature conversion of balances held in FCNR(B) deposits into RFC Accounts by Non-Resident Indians on their return to India.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum percentage penalty a commercial bank can charge for premature withdrawal of FCNR(B) deposits?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any maximum penalty percentage, rate, or cap; it only describes when penalties may or may not be levied and requires board-approved policy.

questions.question: How often must a commercial bank review its Data Quality Index across all reporting segments?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must conduct a half-yearly review of the Data Quality Index for all segments.
questions.evidence: A CI shall undertake half yearly review of the DQI for all segments

questions.question: Within what timeframe must a commercial bank present its DQI review report to top management after each half-year ends?
questions.answer: The report must be placed before top management within two months from the end of the half-year.
questions.evidence: A report consisting of issues identified and corrective steps taken shall be placed before its top management by each CI for review within two months from the end of that half-year.

unanswerable.question: What specific data quality metrics or thresholds must a commercial bank meet for each segment during the DQI review?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph mandates a half-yearly review and reporting to top management but does not define the specific metrics, benchmarks, or acceptable thresholds that constitute the Data Quality Index for any segment.

questions.question: What must an NBFC do if a customer that is a non-profit organisation is not already registered on the DARPAN Portal of NITI Aayog?
questions.answer: The NBFC must register the customer's details on the DARPAN Portal itself.
questions.evidence: If they are not registered, the NBFC shall register the details on the DARPAN Portal.

questions.question: How long must an NBFC retain the DARPAN Portal registration records for a non-profit organisation customer after the relationship ends?
questions.answer: The NBFC must keep the registration records for five years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall also maintain such registration records for a period of five years after the business relationship between the customer and the NBFC has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of onboarding a non-profit organisation must the NBFC complete the DARPAN Portal registration?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit or deadline for completing the registration on the DARPAN Portal.

questions.question: What governance approval is required for a commercial bank's credit card issuance and conduct policy under the RBI Directions?
questions.answer: The policy must be approved by the bank's Board or a Committee delegated by the Board.
questions.evidence: approved by its Board or any Committee to which powers have been delegated by the Board

questions.question: Where must a commercial bank make its credit card policy accessible to the public according to the RBI Directions?
questions.answer: The policy must be available on the card-issuer's website.
questions.evidence: The policy shall be available on the website of the card-issuer.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum time period allowed for a commercial bank to obtain Board approval for its credit card policy after the Directions come into effect?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any deadline or time period for obtaining Board approval.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Standing Sub-Group of the Technical Working Group constituted under the RBI's credit information reporting directions?
questions.answer: The Standing Sub-Group serves as an advisory and collaborative body to provide expert insights and recommendations on technical aspects of credit information reporting, supporting in-depth discussions on challenges faced by credit institutions and credit information companies.
questions.evidence: A Standing Sub-Group of TWG shall be constituted to function as an advisory and collaborative body to offer expert insights and make recommendations on technical aspects of credit information reporting.

questions.question: Does the Standing Sub-Group address required changes to IT systems for credit information reporting formats?
questions.answer: Yes, the Sub-Group's purpose includes supporting discussions on necessary modifications, including changes in IT systems, that may be required in data reporting formats.
questions.evidence: This includes necessary modifications, including changes in the IT systems, that may be required in the data reporting formats.

unanswerable.question: How many members are appointed to the Standing Sub-Group of the Technical Working Group?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph describes the Sub-Group's purpose and functions but does not specify its composition, size, or appointment process.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank provide financial assistance to equipment leasing companies?
questions.answer: Yes, commercial banks are permitted to extend financial assistance to equipment leasing companies.
questions.evidence: As banks can extend financial assistance to equipment leasing companies

questions.question: Is a commercial bank allowed to directly enter into lease agreements with equipment leasing companies or NBFCs engaged in equipment leasing?
questions.answer: No, commercial banks are prohibited from entering into lease agreements departmentally with equipment leasing companies and other NBFCs engaged in equipment leasing.
questions.evidence: they shall not enter into lease agreements departmentally with such companies as well as other NBFCs engaged in equipment leasing

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum tenure for which a commercial bank can provide financial assistance to an equipment leasing company?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any tenure limits, numerical thresholds, or time periods for financial assistance to equipment leasing companies.

questions.question: What additional technology-related factors must a commercial bank evaluate when selecting an IT service provider beyond the standard service provider evaluation?
questions.answer: The bank must assess the provider's technology, infrastructural stability, data backup arrangements, and disaster recovery plan.
questions.evidence: (i) technology, infrastructural stability, data backup arrangements, and disaster recovery plan;

questions.question: How should a commercial bank ensure its data remains protected and accessible when outsourced to an IT service provider?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure appropriate controls, assurance requirements, and contractual arrangements are in place for data protection and the bank's access to data processed, managed, or stored by the provider.
questions.evidence: (vi) ensuring that appropriate controls, assurance requirements, and possible contractual arrangements are in place to ensure data protection and bank's access to the data which is processed, managed or stored by the service provider;

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum allowable downtime for an IT service provider's disaster recovery plan under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists disaster recovery plan as an evaluation factor but does not specify any numerical thresholds, time limits, or recovery time objectives.

questions.question: Can the Reserve Bank of India grant a commercial bank an extension of time to comply with the Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: Yes, the RBI may grant an extension of time to comply with or exempt a commercial bank from all or any provisions of the Directions, either generally or for a specified period.
questions.evidence: The Reserve Bank may, if it considers necessary for avoiding any hardship or for any other just and sufficient reason, grant extension of time to comply with or exempt any regulated entity, from all or any of the provisions of these Directions either generally or for any specified period

questions.question: Are there any conditions that the Reserve Bank of India can impose when granting an exemption to a commercial bank under the Digital Banking Channels Authorisation Directions, 2025?
questions.answer: Yes, the RBI may impose such conditions as it deems fit when granting an exemption or extension of time.
questions.evidence: subject to such conditions as the Reserve Bank may impose.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum duration for which the Reserve Bank of India can grant an exemption to a commercial bank under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states exemptions can be granted "for any specified period" but does not specify a maximum duration or limit.

questions.question: Where should a commercial bank look for the meaning of a term used in the RBI Credit Information Reporting Directions if that term is not defined in the Directions themselves?
questions.answer: The bank should first refer to the CICRA, 2005, the Credit Information Companies Rules, 2006, and the CIC Regulations; if the term is not defined there, it should then refer to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, or the Companies Act, 2013.
questions.evidence: Words or expressions used in these Directions and not defined herein, but defined in CICRA, 2005, the Credit Information Companies Rules, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'CIC Rules') and the CIC Regulations, shall have the same meanings as assigned to them in these Statute/ Rules/ Regulations. Any other words or expressions used and not defined in these directions or aforesaid Statute/ Rules/ Regulations and defined in Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 or Banking Regulation Act, 1949 or the Companies Act, 2013 shall have the same meanings as assigned to them in these Acts.

questions.question: Which specific Acts provide the final fallback definitions for words used in the Credit Information Reporting Directions that are not defined in the Directions, CICRA, CIC Rules, or CIC Regulations?
questions.answer: The Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, and the Companies Act, 2013 serve as the final sources for definitions of such terms.
questions.evidence: Any other words or expressions used and not defined in these directions or aforesaid Statute/ Rules/ Regulations and defined in Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 or Banking Regulation Act, 1949 or the Companies Act, 2013 shall have the same meanings as assigned to them in these Acts.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of business days a commercial bank has to reconcile its internal definitions with the hierarchy set out in the Directions after a new term is introduced?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only establishes the hierarchy of definitions across statutes and regulations; it does not specify any timeline, deadline, or procedural requirement for banks to update or reconcile their internal glossaries.

questions.question: What internal benchmark must a commercial bank use to price floating rate rupee loans that are sanctioned or renewed on or after April 1, 2016?
questions.answer: The bank must use the Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) as the internal benchmark for pricing such loans.
questions.evidence: All floating rate rupee loans sanctioned and renewed w.e.f. April 1, 2016 shall be priced with reference to the Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR) which will be the internal benchmark

questions.question: From what date does the requirement to price floating rate rupee loans using MCLR apply for a commercial bank?
questions.answer: The requirement applies to all floating rate rupee loans sanctioned and renewed with effect from April 1, 2016.
questions.evidence: All floating rate rupee loans sanctioned and renewed w.e.f. April 1, 2016 shall be priced with reference to the Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate (MCLR)

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible spread that a commercial bank can charge over the MCLR for floating rate rupee loans?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that MCLR is the internal benchmark and that pricing must be with reference to it, but does not specify any limits, caps, or rules regarding the spread or margin over MCLR.

questions.question: Do the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks – Digital Banking Channels Authorisation) Directions, 2025 override or replace existing banking laws and regulations?
questions.answer: No, the Directions are in addition to and not in derogation of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions currently in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: If a commercial bank complies with these Directions, does it still need to comply with other applicable banking regulations?
questions.answer: Yes, compliance with these Directions does not relieve a commercial bank from complying with other applicable laws, rules, regulations, or directions.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific timeline for commercial banks to align their existing digital banking channels with these Directions without violating other regulations?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any timeline, deadline, or transition period for compliance alignment with other laws.

questions.question: What is the maximum share of total assets that an NBFC which is not registered as an NBFC-MFI may allocate to microfinance loans?
questions.answer: Such an NBFC may extend microfinance loans only up to 25 per cent of its total assets in aggregate.
questions.evidence: An NBFC, which does not qualify as an NBFC-MFI shall extend microfinance loans, which in aggregate does not exceed 25 per cent of its total assets.

questions.question: Which other RBI directions govern microfinance loans for all NBFCs, including NBFC-MFIs?
questions.answer: Microfinance loans are guided by the RBI Directions on Credit Facilities, Responsible Business Conduct, and Managing Risks in Outsourcing for NBFCs, as amended.
questions.evidence: Microfinance loans of all NBFCs including NBFC-MFIs shall be guided by the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025, Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Responsible Business Conduct) Directions, 2025, and Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Managing Risks in Outsourcing) Directions, 2025, as amended from time to time.

unanswerable.question: What supervisory action or penalty applies if a non-NBFC-MFI exceeds the 25 per cent microfinance loan limit?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph sets the 25 per cent ceiling but does not specify any enforcement measure, penalty, or remedial timeline for breaching it.

questions.question: If a commercial bank took action under the previous interest rate directions before they were repealed, does that action remain valid under the new 2025 Directions?
questions.answer: Yes, any action taken or initiated under the repealed directions continues to be governed by those provisions.
questions.evidence: any action taken or purported to have been taken, or initiated under the repealed Directions, instructions, or guidelines shall continue to be governed by the provisions thereof.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank still be penalized for a contravention committed under the repealed interest rate directions after the new 2025 Directions take effect?
questions.answer: Yes, the repeal does not affect penalties incurred for contraventions under the repealed directions, and such penalties may be imposed as if the repeal had not occurred.
questions.evidence: any such penalty, forfeiture or punishment may be imposed as if those directions, instructions, or guidelines had not been repealed.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific deadline by which commercial banks must transition their existing loan pricing models to comply with the new 2025 Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any transition deadline; it only states that actions under repealed directions continue to be governed by them.

questions.question: Which Reserve Bank of India directions on credit facilities must an NBFC-MFI comply with?
questions.answer: An NBFC-MFI must comply with the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Credit Facilities) Directions, 2025.

questions.question: Which specific paragraphs of the RBI's Financial Services Directions apply to an NBFC-MFI?
questions.answer: An NBFC-MFI must adhere to paragraphs 6 to 14, 23 to 33, and 50 to 57 of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Undertaking of Financial Services) Directions, 2025.
questions.evidence: Paragraphs 6 to 14, 23 to 33 and 50 to 57 of Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies – Undertaking of Financial Services) Directions, 2025.

unanswerable.question: What is the deadline for an NBFC-MFI to implement the Credit Cards Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only states that NBFC-MFIs shall adhere to the Credit Cards Directions but does not specify any implementation deadline or transition period.

questions.question: When is an NBFC required to release securities held as collateral for a loan?
questions.answer: An NBFC must release all securities when the borrower repays all dues or the outstanding loan amount is realized, unless the NBFC has a legitimate right or lien for other claims against the borrower.
questions.evidence: An NBFC shall release all securities on repayment of all dues or on realisation of the outstanding amount of loan subject to any legitimate right or lien for any other claim they may have against borrower.

questions.question: What information must an NBFC provide to a borrower if it retains securities under a right of set-off?
questions.answer: The NBFC must give the borrower notice with full particulars about the remaining claims and the conditions under which it is entitled to retain the securities until those claims are settled or paid.
questions.evidence: If such right of set off is to be exercised, the borrower shall be given notice about the same with full particulars about the remaining claims and the conditions under which the NBFC is entitled to retain the securities till the relevant claim is settled / paid.

unanswerable.question: How many days does an NBFC have to issue the set-off notice to the borrower after deciding to retain securities?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the NBFC to give notice with full particulars but does not specify any time limit or deadline for providing that notice.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank establish to ensure fair application of penal provisions for wilful defaulters?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must put in place a transparent mechanism for the entire process of identification of wilful defaulters.
questions.evidence: A bank shall put in place a transparent mechanism for the entire process of identification of wilful defaulters so that the penal provisions are applied in a fair manner and the scope for discretion is obviated.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the transparent mechanism that a commercial bank must implement for identifying wilful defaulters?
questions.answer: The mechanism ensures penal provisions are applied fairly and eliminates discretion in the identification process.
questions.evidence: A bank shall put in place a transparent mechanism for the entire process of identification of wilful defaulters so that the penal provisions are applied in a fair manner and the scope for discretion is obviated.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific deadline by which a commercial bank must have the transparent mechanism for identifying wilful defaulters fully operational?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any timeline, deadline, or implementation date for the transparent mechanism.

questions.question: For a public sector bank, who is eligible to serve on the Nomination and Remuneration Committee?
questions.answer: Only non-executive directors may serve, but the Government of India nominee director and the director nominated under the specified SBI Act or Banking Companies Acts are excluded.
questions.evidence: A PSB shall constitute a Nomination and Remuneration Committee (NRC) consisting of only NEDs. The Government of India nominee director and the director nominated under Section 19(f) of the SBI Act / Section 9(3)(c) of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1970 / 1980 shall not be part of the Committee.

questions.question: What are the quorum and chairing requirements for a Nomination and Remuneration Committee meeting in a public sector bank?
questions.answer: The NRC requires a quorum of three members, at least half of whom must be independent directors including one from the Risk Management Committee of the Board, and the meeting must be chaired by an independent director.
questions.evidence: The NRC shall meet with a quorum of three members. At least half of the members attending the meeting of the NRC shall be independent directors, of which one shall be a member of the RMCB. The meetings of the NRC shall be chaired by an independent director.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of members permitted on the Nomination and Remuneration Committee of a public sector bank?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies composition rules and quorum but does not state an upper limit on committee size.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank permitted to pay additional interest to its retired staff members who are resident Indian senior citizens, on top of the interest benefit they already receive as retired employees?
questions.answer: Yes, a commercial bank may at its discretion provide additional interest rates admissible to senior citizens to its resident Indian retired staff who are senior citizens, over and above the additional interest payable to them as retired staff.
questions.evidence: A bank may, at its discretion, give its resident Indian retired staffs, who are senior citizens, the benefit of additional interest rates as admissible to senior citizens over and above the additional interest payable to them by virtue of their being retired members of the bank’s staff.

questions.question: Which category of retired bank staff qualifies for the extra senior citizen interest benefit under the RBI directions?
questions.answer: Only resident Indian retired staff who are senior citizens qualify for the additional interest rates admissible to senior citizens over and above their staff benefit.
questions.evidence: A bank may, at its discretion, give its resident Indian retired staffs, who are senior citizens, the benefit of additional interest rates as admissible to senior citizens over and above the additional interest payable to them by virtue of their being retired members of the bank’s staff.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible additional interest rate that a commercial bank may offer to its retired senior citizen staff beyond the standard staff benefit?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that a bank may give the benefit but does not specify any maximum rate, cap, or limit on the additional interest payable.

questions.question: What responsibilities does the Board of Directors of an NBFC-P2P lending platform have regarding the Fair Practices Code and grievances redressal mechanism?
questions.answer: The Board must provide for periodic review of compliance with the Fair Practices Code and the functioning of the grievances redressal mechanism at various management levels.
questions.evidence: The Board of Directors shall also provide for periodic review of the compliance of the Fair Practices Code and the functioning of the grievances redressal mechanism at various levels of management.

questions.question: How frequently must the consolidated report on these reviews be submitted to the Board?
questions.answer: The report must be submitted at regular intervals as prescribed by the Board itself.
questions.evidence: A consolidated report of such reviews shall be submitted to the Board at regular intervals, as may be prescribed by it.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days allowed between the periodic reviews?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires periodic reviews but does not specify any maximum interval or deadline.

questions.question: What must an NBFC do when it suspects fraudulent activity in a credit facility or loan account?
questions.answer: The NBFC must conduct either an external audit or an internal audit, following its Board-approved policy, to investigate the account further.
questions.evidence: the Applicable NBFC shall use an external audit or an internal audit as per its Board approved Policy for further investigation in such accounts

questions.question: Who determines whether an external or internal audit is used for investigating suspected fraud at an NBFC?
questions.answer: The NBFC's Board-approved policy governs the choice between an external audit or an internal audit for such investigations.
questions.evidence: the Applicable NBFC shall use an external audit or an internal audit as per its Board approved Policy

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum number of days an NBFC has to initiate an audit after detecting suspicion of fraud?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any time limit or deadline for initiating the audit.

questions.question: What are the four major roles that a public sector bank's Board must fulfil under the RBI governance directions?
questions.answer: The Board must oversee the bank's risk profile, monitor the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensure expert management, and maximise the interests of its stakeholders.
questions.evidence: A PSB's Board shall fulfil four major roles viz. overseeing the risk profile of the PSB, monitoring the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensuring the expert management, and maximising the interests of its stakeholders.

questions.question: Which aspect of a public sector bank's operations must its Board oversee as part of its risk governance role?
questions.answer: The Board must oversee the risk profile of the public sector bank.
questions.evidence: A PSB's Board shall fulfil four major roles viz. overseeing the risk profile of the PSB, monitoring the integrity of its business and control mechanisms, ensuring the expert management, and maximising the interests of its stakeholders.

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum number of board meetings per year required for a public sector bank's Board to discharge these four major roles?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists the four major roles of a PSB's Board but does not specify any meeting frequency, quorum, or procedural requirements for fulfilling them.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, do the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 override previous RBI licensing conditions, notifications, and guidelines that conflict with them?
questions.answer: Yes, the Directions apply notwithstanding anything to the contrary in previous RBI issuances such as licensing conditions, notifications, directions, regulations, guidelines, and instructions issued before these Directions.
questions.evidence: shall be applicable notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in the licensing conditions, notifications, directions, regulations, guidelines, instructions, etc., issued by RBI before the issue of these Directions.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at a commercial bank, must the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025 be read together with other governing statutes?
questions.answer: Yes, the contents of the Master Direction shall be read along with other relevant governing statutes.
questions.evidence: The contents of this Master Direction shall be read along with other relevant governing statutes

unanswerable.question: Which specific governing statutes must be read along with the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks - Governance) Directions, 2025?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the Directions must be read with 'other relevant governing statutes' but does not enumerate or identify which statutes those are.

questions.question: Can a commercial bank initiate recovery proceedings against a guarantor immediately upon default by the principal borrower, or must it first exhaust all remedies against the borrower?
questions.answer: A commercial bank can proceed against the guarantor even without exhausting remedies against the principal debtor, and the guarantor's liability is immediate upon the bank's claim.
questions.evidence: When a default happens in making payment / repayment by the principal debtor, a bank shall be able to proceed against the guarantor even without exhausting the remedies against the principal debtor. Where a bank has made a claim on the guarantor on account of the default made by the principal debtor, the liability of the guarantor is immediate.

questions.question: What are the consequences for a guarantor who refuses to honour a commercial bank's demand for payment after the principal borrower defaults?
questions.answer: The guarantor may be considered for classification as a wilful defaulter by following the mechanism set out in Paragraphs 5 and 6 of the Directions.
questions.evidence: In case the said guarantor refuses to comply with the demand made by the bank, such guarantor shall also be considered for classification as a wilful defaulter by following the mechanism as set out in Paragraphs 5 and 6.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank complete the wilful defaulter classification process for a non-compliant guarantor after making a demand?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that a non-compliant guarantor shall be considered for classification per the mechanism in Paragraphs 5 and 6, but does not specify any timeline or deadline for completing that process.

questions.question: What governance requirement must a commercial bank meet regarding its interest rate policy on advances?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must have a comprehensive policy on interest rates on advances, including microfinance loan pricing, approved by its Board of Directors or a delegated committee.
questions.evidence: There shall be a comprehensive policy duly approved by the Board of Directors or any committee of the Board to which powers have been delegated, in respect of interest rates on advances, including the pricing of microfinance loans.

questions.question: How must a commercial bank price its floating rate loans, excluding those referenced in paragraph 45?
questions.answer: All floating rate loans, except those mentioned in paragraph 45, must be priced with reference to a benchmark as specified in paragraphs 10 to 27.
questions.evidence: All floating rate loans, except those mentioned in paragraph 45, shall be priced with reference to a benchmark as mentioned in paragraphs 10 to 27.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum spread a commercial bank may add to the reference benchmark rate for floating rate loans?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only requires that the lending rate be determined by adding components of spread to the benchmark, but does not prescribe any limit on the spread.

questions.question: For a commercial bank, which MCLR applies to a loan when the first disbursement is only partial?
questions.answer: The MCLR prevailing on the date of that first partial disbursement applies until the next reset date, even if the benchmark changes before then.
questions.evidence: The MCLR prevailing on the date of first disbursement, whether partial or full, shall be applicable till the next reset date, irrespective of the changes in the benchmark during the interim.

questions.question: If the external benchmark changes between the first disbursement and the next reset date, must a commercial bank adjust the loan interest rate immediately?
questions.answer: No, the rate stays fixed at the MCLR from the first disbursement date until the next scheduled reset, regardless of interim benchmark movements.
questions.evidence: The MCLR prevailing on the date of first disbursement, whether partial or full, shall be applicable till the next reset date, irrespective of the changes in the benchmark during the interim.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum allowable interval between reset dates for MCLR-linked loans under these Directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states that future reset dates shall be determined accordingly but does not specify any maximum period, frequency, or deadline for resets.

questions.question: What must an NBFC-P2P do regarding a Fair Practices Code and Board approval?
questions.answer: An NBFC-P2P must establish a Fair Practices Code based on the Guidelines in the Directions and obtain approval for it from its Board.
questions.evidence: An NBFC-P2P shall put in place a Fair Practices Code, based on the Guidelines outlined herein, with the approval of its Board.

questions.question: Where is an NBFC-P2P required to publish its Fair Practices Code?
questions.answer: The Fair Practices Code must be posted on the NBFC-P2P's website so that stakeholders can access it.
questions.evidence: The same should be put up on its website, for the information of various stakeholders.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days of receiving its licence must an NBFC-P2P publish the Board-approved Fair Practices Code on its website?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph states the code must be put on the website but does not specify any deadline or time limit for doing so.

questions.question: For an FCNR(B) deposit renewed within 14 days of maturity, which interest rate applies — the rate on the maturity date or the rate when the depositor requests renewal?
questions.answer: The lower of the two rates applies: the rate prevailing on the original maturity date or the rate on the date the depositor seeks renewal.
questions.evidence: the rate of interest payable on the amount of the deposit so renewed shall be the appropriate rate of interest for the period of renewal as prevailing on the date of maturity or on the date when the depositor seeks renewal, whichever is lower

questions.question: Can a bank authorised under FEMA 1999 recover interest paid for the overdue period if an FCNR(B) deposit is withdrawn before completing the minimum stipulated period after renewal?
questions.answer: Yes, the bank may, at its discretion, recover the interest paid for the overdue period in such cases.
questions.evidence: a bank authorised under FEMA, 1999, may, at its discretion, recover the interest paid for the overdue period, i.e., period beyond the original date of maturity

unanswerable.question: What is the minimum stipulated period under the FCNR(B) Scheme that a renewed deposit must complete before withdrawal to avoid interest recovery?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph mentions a 'minimum stipulated period under the Scheme' but does not specify its duration or define it.

questions.question: What must a commercial bank that issues credit or debit cards do to prevent incorrect billing?
questions.answer: The bank must ensure that wrong bills are not raised and issued to cardholders.
questions.evidence: Card-issuers shall ensure that wrong bills are not raised and issued to cardholders.

questions.question: Within how many days must a commercial bank respond with an explanation and evidence when a cardholder disputes a bill?
questions.answer: The bank must provide an explanation and any applicable documentary evidence within a maximum of 30 days from the date of the complaint.
questions.evidence: the card-issuer shall provide explanation and, wherever applicable, documentary evidence shall be provided to the cardholder within a maximum period of 30 days from the date of complaint.

unanswerable.question: What penalties apply if a commercial bank fails to respond to a billing dispute within the 30-day period?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any penalties, sanctions, or consequences for non-compliance with the 30-day response requirement.

questions.question: How often must a commercial bank report wilful defaulters to credit information companies, and what information must be included in the report?
questions.answer: A commercial bank must submit monthly reports in Annex II format containing two lists: wilful defaulters in suit-filed accounts and wilful defaulters in non-suit-filed accounts.
questions.evidence: A bank shall submit at monthly intervals, information in Annex II to all credit information companies in respect of the wilful defaulters: 1. a list of wilful defaulters (LWD) in respect of suit filed accounts 2. a LWD in respect of non-suit filed accounts

questions.question: Within what timeframe must a commercial bank notify credit information companies when a wilful defaulter's outstanding amount falls below the reporting threshold?
questions.answer: The bank must inform all credit information companies of the removal promptly and not later than thirty days from when the outstanding amount falls below ₹25 lakh or the threshold notified by RBI.
questions.evidence: The bank shall inform all credit information companies the removal of the name of the wilful defaulter from the LWD, promptly and not later than thirty days, from the date when the outstanding amount falls below the threshold of ₹25 lakh or as notified by Reserve Bank of India from time to time

unanswerable.question: What specific data fields or format requirements are prescribed in Annex II for reporting wilful defaulters to credit information companies?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph references Annex II but does not specify its contents, structure, or data field requirements.

questions.question: Is a commercial bank allowed to finance the construction of a building intended solely for a Municipal office?
questions.answer: No, unless the loan is for an activity that will be refinanced by institutions such as NABARD.
questions.evidence: Construction of buildings meant purely for Government / Semi-Government offices, including Municipal and Panchayat offices. However, the bank may grant loans for activities, which will be refinanced by institutions like NABARD.

questions.question: How must a commercial bank calculate its maximum financing for a housing project run by a corporate body that receives government subsidies or capital contributions?
questions.answer: The bank must limit its finance to the total project cost minus the government subsidy or capital contribution and any other government-provided resources.
questions.evidence: the bank finance shall be restricted to an amount arrived at after reducing from the total project cost the amount of subsidy / capital contribution receivable from the Government and any other resources proposed to be made available by the Government.

unanswerable.question: What is the maximum permissible loan-to-value ratio for housing loans granted to intermediary agencies under these directions?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any loan-to-value ratios or limits for housing intermediary agencies; it only lists prohibited financing categories and a restriction on government-subsidized projects.

questions.question: As an NBFC operating under the Account Aggregator framework, do I still need to follow all other applicable laws and regulations in addition to these Directions?
questions.answer: Yes, the Directions explicitly state they are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions currently in force.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

questions.question: Can the Account Aggregator Directions override or replace existing legal requirements that apply to my NBFC?
questions.answer: No, the Directions cannot override or replace other legal requirements; they operate alongside them without diminishing their effect.
questions.evidence: The provisions of these Directions shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of the provisions of any other laws, rules, regulations, or directions, for the time being in force.

unanswerable.question: What is the specific deadline by which NBFCs must complete their compliance review of all other applicable laws after these Directions come into effect?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph does not specify any deadline, time period, or procedural requirement for reviewing compliance with other laws.
